children: Texas' factory sector gained steam in August as multiple measures of manufacturing activity pointed to faster growth and perceptions of broader business activity continued to improve, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas.
The Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey's index for general business activity, released by the Dallas Fed, was 11.6 in August following a 1.3 reading in July.

The production index, a key measure of state manufacturing conditions, climbed six points to 16.1, a reading suggestive of an above-average pace of output expansion. The company outlook index rose to 19.2 from 13.4, signaling a notable improvement in outlooks.
The new orders index jumped 16 points to a reading of 22. Employment growth slowed slightly in August, while work hours were stable.
Meanwhile, the raw materials prices index increased three points and the finished goods prices index fell three points to 22.7.
